description: The physics of the very small. Covers wave-particle duality, the Schrodinger equation, quantum states in Hilbert space, angular momentum, spin, identical particles, and perturbation theory.

concepts.title: The Failures of Classical Physics
learning_objectives: Describe the ultraviolet catastrophe and how Planck's quantization hypothesis resolves it
Explain the photoelectric effect and Einstein's photon hypothesis
Describe the Compton effect and its evidence for particle-like behavior of light

concepts.title: Wave-Particle Duality and the de Broglie Hypothesis
learning_objectives: State the de Broglie relation λ = h/p and compute the wavelength of matter waves
Describe the Davisson-Germer experiment as evidence for electron diffraction
Explain the double-slit experiment and its implications for quantum superposition

concepts.title: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
learning_objectives: State the position-momentum uncertainty relation Δx Δp ≥ ℏ/2
State the energy-time uncertainty relation ΔE Δt ≥ ℏ/2
Apply uncertainty relations to estimate ground-state energies and explain the stability of atoms

concepts.title: The Time-Dependent Schrodinger Equation
learning_objectives: State the time-dependent Schrodinger equation iℏ ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ
Interpret the wave function ψ(x,t) and the probability density |ψ|²
Apply the normalization condition ∫|ψ|² dx = 1

concepts.title: Separation of Variables and Stationary States
learning_objectives: Separate the time-dependent Schrodinger equation into time-independent and time parts
State the time-independent Schrodinger equation Ĥψ = Eψ as an eigenvalue problem
Express the general solution as a superposition of stationary states

concepts.title: Probability Current and Conservation
learning_objectives: Derive the probability current density j = (ℏ/2mi)(ψ*∇ψ − ψ∇ψ*)
State the continuity equation ∂ρ/∂t + ∇·j = 0 for quantum probability
Apply boundary conditions requiring continuity of ψ and dψ/dx

concepts.title: The Infinite Square Well
learning_objectives: Solve the time-independent Schrodinger equation for the infinite square well
Derive the quantized energy levels Eₙ = n²π²ℏ²/(2mL²)
Normalize the wave functions and verify their orthogonality

concepts.title: The Quantum Harmonic Oscillator
learning_objectives: Solve the harmonic oscillator Schrodinger equation using power series (Hermite polynomials)
Derive the energy spectrum Eₙ = (n + ½)ℏω and discuss the zero-point energy
Sketch the wave functions and probability densities and compare with classical turning points

concepts.title: Free Particle and Wave Packets
learning_objectives: Solve the free-particle Schrodinger equation and express solutions as plane waves
Construct wave packets from superpositions of plane waves using Fourier transforms
Compute and interpret group velocity and phase velocity of a wave packet

concepts.title: Potential Barriers and Quantum Tunneling
learning_objectives: Solve the Schrodinger equation for a finite potential step and barrier
Compute transmission and reflection coefficients
Explain quantum tunneling and apply it to alpha decay and scanning tunneling microscopy

concepts.title: Hilbert Space and Dirac Notation
learning_objectives: Represent quantum states as vectors in Hilbert space using Dirac bra-ket notation
Compute inner products ⟨φ|ψ⟩ and expand states in orthonormal bases
Express the completeness relation and resolution of the identity

concepts.title: Observables and Hermitian Operators
learning_objectives: Represent physical observables as Hermitian operators
Prove that eigenvalues of Hermitian operators are real and eigenstates are orthogonal
Compute expectation values ⟨A⟩ = ⟨ψ|Â|ψ⟩ and standard deviations

concepts.title: The Generalized Uncertainty Principle
learning_objectives: Derive the generalized uncertainty relation ΔA ΔB ≥ ½|⟨[Â,B̂]⟩|
Compute commutators of common operators (x̂, p̂, L̂, Ĥ)
Identify compatible observables (commuting operators) and their simultaneous eigenstates

concepts.title: Time Evolution and the Schrodinger vs Heisenberg Pictures
learning_objectives: Express time evolution using the unitary operator U(t) = e^{−iĤt/ℏ}
State Ehrenfest's theorem relating quantum expectation values to classical equations of motion
Distinguish between the Schrodinger picture and the Heisenberg picture of time evolution

concepts.title: The 3D Schrodinger Equation and Separation in Spherical Coordinates
learning_objectives: Write the time-independent Schrodinger equation in spherical coordinates
Separate the equation into radial and angular parts
Identify the angular solutions as spherical harmonics Yₗᵐ(θ,φ)

concepts.title: Angular Momentum in Quantum Mechanics
learning_objectives: Derive the commutation relations for angular momentum operators [L̂ᵢ, L̂ⱼ] = iℏε_ijk L̂ₖ
Solve the eigenvalue problem for L̂² and L̂_z using ladder operators
Identify the quantum numbers l and m and their allowed values

concepts.title: The Hydrogen Atom
learning_objectives: Solve the radial equation for the Coulomb potential to find hydrogen energy levels Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV
Identify the quantum numbers n, l, m and their relationship to orbitals
Sketch radial wave functions and probability distributions for low-n states

modules.title: Spin and Addition of Angular Momentum

concepts.title: Spin-½ and the Pauli Matrices
learning_objectives: Introduce spin as an intrinsic angular momentum with no classical analog
Represent spin-½ states as two-component spinors and spin operators as Pauli matrices
Compute expectation values and probabilities for spin measurements along arbitrary axes

concepts.title: Addition of Angular Momentum
learning_objectives: Add two angular momenta using Clebsch-Gordan coefficients
Determine the allowed values of total angular momentum quantum numbers
Apply angular momentum addition to spin-orbit coupling in hydrogen

concepts.title: The Stern-Gerlach Experiment and Measurement
learning_objectives: Describe the Stern-Gerlach experiment and its demonstration of spin quantization
Analyze sequential Stern-Gerlach measurements and state collapse
Discuss the measurement problem and the projection postulate

concepts.title: Symmetry of Multi-Particle Wave Functions
learning_objectives: Construct symmetric (bosonic) and antisymmetric (fermionic) multi-particle wave functions
Write the two-particle wave function as a Slater determinant for fermions
Explain exchange degeneracy and its resolution by symmetrization

concepts.title: The Pauli Exclusion Principle and the Periodic Table
learning_objectives: State the Pauli exclusion principle for fermions
Apply the aufbau principle and Hund's rules to determine electron configurations
Explain the structure of the periodic table using quantum numbers and the exclusion principle

concepts.title: Exchange Forces and the Helium Atom
learning_objectives: Describe the exchange interaction and its effect on the energy of multi-electron states
Analyze the ground state and first excited states of helium (singlet and triplet)
Apply variational methods to estimate the ground-state energy of helium

concepts.title: Non-Degenerate Perturbation Theory
learning_objectives: Derive first-order corrections to energy E_n^(1) = ⟨n⁰|Ĥ'|n⁰⟩ and the wave function
Compute second-order energy corrections using summation over unperturbed states
Apply perturbation theory to the ground state of helium (first-order energy correction)

concepts.title: Degenerate Perturbation Theory
learning_objectives: Identify when degenerate perturbation theory is necessary
Diagonalize the perturbation matrix within the degenerate subspace
Apply degenerate perturbation theory to the Stark effect in hydrogen

concepts.title: Fine Structure of Hydrogen
learning_objectives: Calculate the relativistic kinetic energy correction to hydrogen energy levels
Calculate the spin-orbit coupling correction using degenerate perturbation theory
Derive the fine structure formula and compare energy level splittings to spectral data

concepts.title: Time-Dependent Perturbation Theory
learning_objectives: Derive the transition amplitude to first order for a time-dependent perturbation
Apply the result to sudden and adiabatic perturbations
Compute transition probabilities for sinusoidal perturbations

concepts.title: Fermi's Golden Rule
learning_objectives: Derive Fermi's Golden Rule for the transition rate to a continuum of final states
Apply Fermi's Golden Rule to calculate photoelectric effect transition rates
Identify the role of the density of states in determining transition rates

concepts.title: Selection Rules and Spontaneous Emission
learning_objectives: Derive electric dipole selection rules Δl = ±1, Δm = 0, ±1 from matrix elements
Apply Einstein's A and B coefficients to relate spontaneous and stimulated emission
Compute spontaneous emission rates for hydrogen transitions

concepts.title: Quantum Entanglement and Bell's Theorem
learning_objectives: Define entangled states and distinguish them from product states
Derive the Bell (CHSH) inequality from local hidden variable assumptions
Explain how quantum mechanics violates Bell's inequality and the implications for locality

concepts.title: Density Matrices and Mixed States
learning_objectives: Define the density matrix ρ = Σ pᵢ |ψᵢ⟩⟨ψᵢ| for pure and mixed states
Compute expectation values and time evolution using the density matrix
Perform partial traces to describe subsystems of entangled states

concepts.title: Qubits and Quantum Gates
learning_objectives: Represent qubit states on the Bloch sphere
Define and apply common quantum gates (Hadamard, CNOT, Pauli, phase)
Analyze simple quantum circuits and compute output states

projects.title: Numerical Solution of the 1D Schrodinger Equation
projects.description: Implement a numerical solver for the time-independent Schrodinger equation in arbitrary 1D potentials. Compute energy eigenvalues and wave functions for the harmonic oscillator, finite well, and double well, and verify against analytic results.
learning_objectives: Discretize the Schrodinger equation and solve the resulting matrix eigenvalue problem
Validate numerical results against known analytic solutions
Explore the behavior of wave functions in novel potential shapes

projects.title: Computing the Hydrogen Spectrum with Perturbation Theory
projects.description: Calculate the fine structure corrections to hydrogen energy levels using perturbation theory. Compute the Lamb shift qualitatively, and compare theoretical predictions to observed spectral lines.
learning_objectives: Apply both non-degenerate and degenerate perturbation theory to a physical system
Compute relativistic and spin-orbit corrections and compare magnitudes
Match theoretical predictions to experimental spectral data

projects.title: Quantum Teleportation Protocol
projects.description: Work through the quantum teleportation protocol step by step using Dirac notation. Verify that an arbitrary qubit state is faithfully transmitted using entanglement and classical communication.
learning_objectives: Trace through a multi-qubit quantum circuit using bra-ket algebra
Apply quantum gates and measurements to entangled states
Verify that the output state matches the input state after classical correction
